question.worked_solution:
First, we rearrange our equation to isolate the logarithmic term:

$$
\begin{aligned}4{log}_{9}⁡x-2{log}_{9}⁡x & =1 \\ (4-2){log}_{9}⁡x & =1 \\ 2{log}_{9}⁡x & =1 \\ {log}_{9}⁡x & =\frac{1}{2}\end{aligned}
$$

To remove the logarithm, we exponentiate both sides of the equation. The base of the logarithm is $9,$ so we use this base for the exponentiation as well:

$$
\begin{aligned}{log}_{9}⁡x & =\frac{1}{2} \\ {9}^{{log}_{9}⁡x} & ={9}^{1/2}\end{aligned}
$$

Now, since exponentiation is the inverse function of the logarithm, we get ${9}^{{log}_{9}⁡x}=x.$

Therefore,

$$
\begin{aligned}x & ={9}^{1/2} \\ x & =\sqrt{9} \\ x & =3.\end{aligned}
$$
